chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar and 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have made the world between My servants a loan. So whoever lends Me a loan from it, I will give him ten for every one, up to seven hundred times, and whatever I desire from that; and whoever does not lend Me a loan from it, so I take something from him forcibly. If he is patient, I will give him three characteristics, such that if I were to give one of them to My angels, they would be pleased with Me from it.'

He said, then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who, when a misfortune befalls them, say: Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return.'
'Those are they upon whom are blessings from their Lord.' So this (blessings) is one of the three characteristics.
And mercy is the second, and guidance is the third.
Then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is for those from whom Allah takes something forcibly.'

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world, viewed here as a loan
key_terms.الْمُهْتَدُونَ: The guided ones, referring to those who follow the right course
key_terms.قَرْضاً: A loan, metaphor for worldly life or charity
key_terms.قَسْراً: Forcibly, referring to divine decree taking away wealth or health

ai.seo_question: What are the three gifts Allah gives to those who are patient when He takes something from them forcibly?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the dual nature of worldly trials as either a voluntary 'loan' through charity or an involuntary loss through divine decree, rewarding patience in both cases. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly links the three gifts of blessings, mercy, and guidance to Surah Al-Baqarah, highlighting the spiritual elevation of the patient believer. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *sabr* not merely as endurance, but as an active mechanism for acquiring divine proximity and guidance.
